required_outcomes: Treats the email as the door fault coming back on a request closed on 7 June on the understanding the tenant would report a recurrence: reopens it or opens a linked doors job (not Appliances), carrying the earlier history.

Asks the landlord to approve a joiner or door specialist for the front door and frame now, reminding him he offered a contractor visit if needed and that the key method no longer works, and mentioning the frame movement and rattling glass.
Replies to the tenant: acknowledges, says the landlord is being asked to approve a visit, a safety note not to force the door against the glass, and asks her to report at once if it will not lock.
acceptable_alternatives: Raising the priority above routine because the door now takes minutes to secure and the frame moves.
Asking the tenant for photos or a short video of the door closing to brief the contractor.
positive_behaviours: Asks whether the back door, which had the same problem in June, is still the same, and includes it if so.
Sets a dated follow-up for the landlord's answer.
red_flags: Treating the email as a new unrelated request and re-asking the original intake questions.
Escalating to a human when the next step is a routine landlord approval.
prohibited_actions: Telling the tenant to keep using the key method and leaving the email with no repair request.
Assigning a contractor before the landlord approves while the door still locks.
critical_failures: Leaving the recurrence unactioned: no request to the landlord and no reply to the tenant.
